A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same risk-based uncertainty framework despite changes to the title and author list. The complete main texts and appendices, including equations, figures and tables, are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original deep-ensemble evaluations for OOD and misclassification detection on CIFAR datasets and their modified versions, including AUROC results in Section 6 and Appendices G-J.

after.justification: V3 reports original uncertainty evaluations on CIFAR, TinyImageNet and distribution-shift datasets in Section 6 and Appendices J-K, plus numerical illustrations of a Beta-Bernoulli model in Appendix M.

M1.justification: V3 adds central prediction as a third Bayesian approximation strategy alongside v2's risk averaging and posterior predictive averaging. This expands the framework from four to nine combinations for two-argument risks and introduces MBI, MRBI and bias terms (Section 4; Appendix E), substantially extending the uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E1.justification: V3 adds TinyImageNet, ImageNet-A/R/O, CIFAR10C corruption levels 1-5 and a Beta-Bernoulli test case. V2's separately Gaussian-blurred CIFAR10/100 and missing-class CIFAR10 evaluations disappear. The custom label-noised CIFAR datasets persist under the CIFAR10-N/CIFAR100-N names; these are not newly introduced datasets.

E2.justification: Alongside the retained risk-based comparisons, v3 adds two closely related Bayesian energy comparators: energy of expected logits, E(x; Eθfθ), and expected energy, EθE(x; fθ). Their actual OOD and misclassification results appear in Tables 3, 5, 8-10 and 13; v2 has no corresponding energy comparisons.

E3.justification: V2's 20-member ensembles using ResNet18 and VGG19 become five four-member ensembles using ResNet18 in v3. V3 also evaluates pretrained cross-entropy TinyImageNet models and introduces explicit prior/sample-size settings for the toy analysis. AUROC and the documented 200-epoch CIFAR training schedules remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish that retained models were retrained.

E4.justification: V2's extensive matching-versus-mismatching scoring-rule analysis, including exclusion of Neglog and the missing-class disagreement test, is removed. V3 instead emphasizes scoring-function and expanded approximation comparisons, and adds prior sensitivity, sample-size behavior and Gaussian posterior-approximation error analyses (Appendix M, Figures 4-6). Cross-scoring evaluation remains for TinyImageNet.

E5.justification: V2 provides point-valued AUROC tables, ensemble-member distribution plots and some aggregate mean/dispersion summaries in Appendix J. V3 explicitly reports mean AUROC and standard deviation across five independent four-member ensemble groups for individual configurations (Section 6; Appendices J-K). This substantially changes statistical reporting without establishing an increase beyond 20 models.

E6.justification: V3 replaces much of v2's aggregated and matching/nonmatching result set with scoring-rule-specific results under revised ensemble settings, and adds central-prediction, energy and new-dataset outcomes. For example, its new ImageNet-O comparison reports MRBI AUROC 74.46 ± 0.22 versus 72.72 ± 0.33 and 71.15 ± 0.34 for the two energy estimates (Table 3). These are newly reported comparisons, not same-setting gains over v2.

T1.justification: V3 adds central-prediction derivations and the zero-one degeneracy discussion (Appendix L), additional decomposition identities (Appendix F), energy and logit-covariance identities (Section 4.2; Appendix G), and closed-form Beta-Bernoulli uncertainty expressions (Appendix M). V2's original risk derivations and Bayes-risk approximation bound are retained or relocated, rather than newly established.

C1.justification: The main claims about pointwise risks, Bregman divergences and Bayesian generation of uncertainty measures remain. V3 adds the conclusion that energy-based measures fit the framework, while its introduction more explicitly credits earlier work for the underlying risk decomposition. These refine and extend the retained central contribution.

C2.justification: V3 adds substantive explanations of OOD detection through model confidence and disagreement (Appendix A), a noiseless-input qualification (Section 2.2), and prior/posterior misspecification discussions (Appendix M). The original limitations survive in Appendix B. New energy recommendations exceed Table 10's support, and the soft-OOD designation for ImageNet-O is not reconciled with Appendix I.2's description of unseen classes.

D1.justification: V3 supplies a project-specific source-code access statement, identifies the pretrained TinyImageNet model source (Appendix H), and clarifies that label-noised CIFAR training is evaluated on the original datasets (Appendix I.1). The last point is newly documented, not an established change to evaluation data. Existing CIFAR optimizer and training-schedule descriptions largely persist.

R1.justification: V2's brief comparison with Adlam et al. expands into detailed positioning against Gruber and Buettner and the independent work of Hofman et al., including a claimed special-case relationship (Section 5). V3 adds energy-based, credal and generative uncertainty literature while removing much of the second-order-model discussion. This substantially revises research positioning beyond citation-format changes.

P1.justification: V3 rewrites the abstract and contributions, restructures the Bayesian-estimation discussion and experimental questions, and substantially revises related work. It promotes the Bayes-risk bound from an appendix to Section 4.1 and moves limitations into Appendix B. The title, author list, terminology and conference header also change.

P2.justification: V3 substantially redesigns result tables into scoring-rule/estimator grids with mean and standard deviation. Table 1 adds central predictions and removes the Neglog column, whose derivation remains in Appendix D.5. Matching plots disappear, ResNet training plots are merged with a TinyImageNet panel, and new toy-analysis figures appear. The animal illustration and risk diagram are retained and relocated or renumbered.

improvement.justification: V3 better substantiates the framework through central-prediction and energy derivations, closer engagement with prior work, per-configuration variability reporting and explicit sensitivity analyses. These gains are tempered by errors in the added practical guidance: Section 6.4 claims MRBI beats both energy estimates across misclassification datasets, but Table 10 reports 75.51 versus 76.74 and 76.12 on CIFAR100-N. Its ImageNet-O soft-OOD designation also remains unreconciled with the unseen-class description in Appendix I.2. The theoretical development and reporting improve overall, but the new interpretation problems limit the net gain.
